content:
Apple has confirmed it will hold a special product launch event called "Welcome home" next Tuesday (October 13), but has not yet announced whether a keynote video will be released. Here is what we know so far.

Apple has not confirmed a "Welcome home" keynote, but Mark Gurman says there will be an "online video launch event"

Apple has broken from its usual pattern this year, adjusting the way it announces products. The MacBook Neo was the first example — that March launch came after several days of press releases for other products, before being unveiled at an in-person media "experience event."

Now it appears the October 13 "Welcome home" event will also break new ground in a similar fashion.

Unlike traditional events, Apple has not yet added "Welcome home" to its Apple Events webpage, and there is no sign of a livestream on YouTube or the Apple TV app.

With a few days still to go before the event, that could change. But for now, the signs point to no keynote video on October 13.

However, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says there will be a video launch event. In another report about an October 27 Apple event, he wrote:

In other words, according to Gurman (who previously accurately reported the October 13 date and that the event would focus on smart home products), Apple will hold an "online video launch event" next week.

Media will attend the "Apple Experience" event in New York, starting at 9 a.m. Eastern Time. So if there is a launch video, we will most likely see it premiere online around that time — much earlier than a typical keynote.

We are expecting at least three new products on Tuesday — you can read about them here.

Do you think Apple will release a keynote video for "Welcome home"? Let us know in the comments.
